utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General. If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have but a few questions to ask you. From the period of May through July of 1998, did you know any individuals who were involved in fighting whose name was Shala?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall - I'm sure you do, since there's been a fair amount of discussion concerning this matter - being involved in an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2003?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Present at that interview were yourself; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As well as a number of members of the Prosecution team, including Ole Lehtinen, an investigator, Colin Black, a prosecutor, and an interpreter; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that interview process, questions were put to you by Mr. Lehtinen, the investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor, translated into the language of Albanian to which you responded; true?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I understood your testimony correctly, you were responsible for the Shkoza unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor on November 19th, you were asked about military structure, were you not?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were asked the following question by Mr. Lehtinen with regard to the issue of military structure, were you not? "I know" -- this is Mr. Lehtinen: "I know that there was no actual military structure, but through no military structure, and I'm trying to figure out what -- if this were units, what was the next higher level? Did you have a higher command for these units?" Which is to be found on page 22 of the English translation. And I'm not sure whether you need to review the Albanian. Do you remember that question being asked of you?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could ask the question again. And I don't have the transcript here, so if I could have that to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's probably around page ten or 11 in the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question that I asked you was: Were you asked the following question by Mr. Lehtinen from the Office of the Prosecutor with regard to the issue of military structure? "Q. I know that there was no actual military structure, but you know military structure and I'm trying to figure out what -- if this were units, what was the next higher level? Did you have a higher command for these units?" That was a question that was asked of you by Mr. Lehtinen; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You responded to that question by stating: "The General Staff was on top of it"; true?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Mr. Lehtinen, in asking you questions with regard to the issue once again of military structure continued asking you the following: "Q. So there was no -- there was nothing between the General Staff and these units"; correct? That was a question that he asked you?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you responded: "There wasn't yet a middle step or another step. There was at that time -- so were there -- there was no other step between the General Staff and the units. But then we got the order at a later time, got the order that these units had to be turned into brigades." That was your answer; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen at that time changed his questioning to you, from that dealing specifically with the issue of military structure to the timing of structure, to the time that things occurred. And the next question he asked you was as follows: "Q. Okay. But this only happened after, after July 1998"; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You responded to that question, in which you explained: "A. Before -- before -- acting before that, we were all friends with each other, so we had contacts with each other. That's how we communicated about everything. Somewhere around the middle of May 1998, so we -- all the unit -- people responsible for the units got together around the middle of 1998" -- I'm sorry -- "Around the middle of May 1998 to find somebody who would be responsible for all the zones, the General Staff to create zones and complete them as well, inside the zones, and to send a representative there. Since the death of our legendary commander there had been nobody substituting him"; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And from May 1998 through the summer months you were engaged in many, many different activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were defending the population; true?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were establishing ambulance brigades; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were trying to assist the displaced people, people who had been driven from their homes by the Serbs; true?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were attempting to organise as best you could; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, of course, throughout all of this, you were fighting for your lives and for the lives of your people; correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I fought and I tried as best as I could to protect the population and to fight for my country.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Talking again about the Shkoza units, I'd direct your attention to the time early on, just after mid-March 1998. You talked earlier about being based in Acareva at this time. How many Shkoza units were there in March and May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, there was only one. But until May, there were two or three units, Shkoza.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that -- and what were their names? Can you describe how they were identified?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shkoza 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And in June, were there any additional Shkoza units added?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. In May, which units were you responsible for?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until I was a commander of the area, of the zone, I was responsible only for this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Which unit?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Shkoza unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to be clear. Which Shkoza unit? Shkoza 1, 2, or 3?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used to communicate. When I was with Shkoza 1, we communicated by radio. In the beginning, I had two or three soldiers. Then we had some other soldiers, and we communicated with Shkoza 1 and Shkoza 2. It was a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And with this group - let's talk about the end of May - which units were under your command?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shkoza 1, the Shkoza unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until I became commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And tell us again, just for the record here, when you became commander.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And before you became that -- were promoted to that command at the end of May, what were the names of the other -- the commanders of the other Shkoza units?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were several friends that we acted together. There was Avni Hoxha, Hysni Shabani. I can't remember all the names but we acted together. We operated together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And by the end of June, which units were under your command?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the end of June, after I became a commander -- what do you mean? After I became a commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you name those units at that time, at the end of June, all the units which were under your command?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was appointed commander of the Drenica zone, we started to unite all the units into a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, my question was: Can you please name all the units which were under your command at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, until these units existed as units, I was not commander of all those units. But when they united together in a brigade, the Alpha, the Guri, the Mali, the Pellumbi, the Sandokan, all these became one as a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder, General, whether you could help me with a little matter about this time that you became commander of the Drenica zone. I understand that that was about the end of May of 1998? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At that time, were there any military police in the Drenica zone?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were thinking of creating a military police, but it had not been structured yet as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that, as I understand from what you're saying, there would have been no military police in the Drenica zone in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1998, before I took the duty of the commander, there were no military police. When I took this responsibility as a commander of the zone, I also took the responsibility of organising the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you know of the presence of military police in any other zone in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no awareness of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Who would have been commander of the Drenica zone in the middle of 19 -- of May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, of the Drenica zone, of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Middle of March?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Middle of May 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed by the General Staff as a commander of the Drenica zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you issue any order or instruction as a programme for military police in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, because when the decision came from the General Staff, after all the units got together and were forming a brigade and a zone and the proposal came from the General Staff, I started upon their decision to create the zone but also create the military police. But as I said, the brigades as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm confused, you see, by your evidence as to when these various things happened. I am particularly interested about the middle of May 1998. And I understand from what you've just said you may then have issued an order in respect of military police, an order described as a programme for military police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean that already by the middle of May 1998 there was an instruction or an order from the General Staff for there to be military police units?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And was there already an instruction by that time for there to be brigades formed?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the brigades began to be formed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever in May of 1998 issue an instruction that a person who left the front line would be imprisoned by the military police?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would that have occurred?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I'm speaking frankly here. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why I'm asking this is you -- I rather understood from your evidence yesterday that military police was something that occurred much later, perhaps September of 1998, and yet some of the other parts of your evidence suggested that it could be earlier. And from what you're now saying, that might have been as early as the middle of May 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to be clear, our strategy was -- even before I became a commander, the strategy was for us to develop, to unite, to create an army. Because we had separate groups, and very often with commanders of the points, of the units, or the fire points, as we called them, we discussed things together and we discussed about the creation of brigades, of the police, and so on. This was how it was. And this procedure continued until the end of 1998, because we couldn't consolidate ourselves. We were fighting all the time, and the conditions were such that we couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The purpose of my questions arises from the document that has been placed before us, which is at tab 13. And I wonder if the witness could be shown that in the form that is in the Albanian language. Is that a document that you recognise, General?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The copy that I have in front of me here is not very clear. It's not clearly legible. I can't see the signature here. Do you have another copy that I could see better?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can try to blow it up perhaps on Sanction, Your Honour, or try to retrieve the actual original from the evidence vault possibly. However, it may assist, the witness does speak quite good English. He may be able to -- it may help him to look at the English version as well for the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if you can attempt on Sanction, and in the meantime, General, if you would look at the English version, in case that assists you.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear to me what's written here, but I'm not clear about the signature, who's the person that has signed this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. That is not clear, I think, to any of us. I understood from your evidence -- your answers a little while ago, though, that you would have been the commander of Drenica in the middle of May 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The talks and the meetings continued until the middle of May. It was by the end of May that I was appointed commander of the zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Who was the commander before you?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before me, it was Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He had died, as I understand it, in March. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm wondering who might have issued an order on the 13th of May, 1998 as commander of Drenica.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question, but until the end of May I was not appointed by the General Staff as a commander -- as the commander of the zone. I don't know who has signed this. I would like to see the original and say who has been the one that has signed this document. If it has been me, I would say that it's been me. It's illegible here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder if we could go to the content of it. The first item of the programme is one that "A soldier who leaves the front line without permission of the commander will be imprisoned by the military police."

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that in accordance with your understanding of things in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was still confusion that was reigning, and we were still in the process of structuring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see. The sixth item is that "If soldiers attempt to cause problems for the police, the police have the right to use physical force against the soldier." Is that in accordance with your understanding of the position in the middle of May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll say it again: I see the contents of this document, but I don't know who signed this. It might be that I have never -- I had never seen this document before. So if somebody could bring the original for me to see who signed this document, it would be better. I'm not sure who signed this document as a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree very much with you that one question is: Who did sign it? But I am asking beyond that to try and understand the time table, as it were, that I understood from your evidence about military police and what this document seems to suggest. And it seems to suggest that there was an existence of military police and a programme for them as early as the middle of May 1998. And that's why I'm asking whether that accords with your understanding of the situation in May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe this document would form the basis of the work of the military police, when it started to work, and they might work upon this document when they operated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles, that was an issue that was of interest to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think most directly affects the cross-examination on behalf of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And because of that, if you wished, we would certainly allow you to reopen your cross-examination on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I was about to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: -- the Chamber if I could be granted leaf to ask one or two questions on behalf of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: General, could I ask one or two questions arising out of the questions put to you of the Trial Chamber. It's right, isn't it, General, that these zones were developing at different rates within Kosovo during 1998, the KLA zones?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... some developing faster than others.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, General, that the Drenica zone, the zone for which you were the commander, was the fastest developing zone?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: And that you became the commander of that zone in May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: And that one of the things that you wished to develop in that zone were -- was the establishment of a military police unit.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: That it's possible that efforts were taken to establish such a unit in May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were efforts, as I said, efforts about the military police, the military hospital, the brigades. Everything was being organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, General, that the situation in the other zones within Kosovo may have been very different to that within Drenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. All the zones were different from each other. They had different problems to tackle with.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: It's -- maybe you can help with this, General, that a time came within the conflict in Kosovo that a military police formation was established that was a unified military police for the KLA that covered the whole of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later -- I don't know whether they covered the whole of Kosovo, but I know that they covered Drenica later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: And when would that be?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean only about the territory of Drenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Drenica and a more -- if you could deal first with Drenica.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll speak about Drenica because I was there myself and I was a protagonist there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as soon as I was appointed a commander, I started the process. Very often we were not able to consolidate, but we tried our best.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: It may be something that you can't help with, General, but can you assist the Trial Chamber with saying when, if at all, a more unified Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. military police formation was established for the whole of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It would be better if somebody from the General Staff answered that question. I don't know. I'm not clear about the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Powles. Mr. Nicholls, is there anything that you would wish to raise by further re-examination arising from that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Not yet at this moment, Your Honour, but it appears that in a moment we may be able to have a better original with a -- which was translated separately, but it's the same document. Mr. Younis is trying to find that at the moment. It should be shortly, if we can compare these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We actually might wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Or possibly, Your Honour, if we could adjourn for five or ten minutes, we'd then be able to also get hard copies and ensure that this is the same document, the same translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the circumstances, we will adjourn, then, and resume hopefully by quarter past?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. --- Break taken at 3.07 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been able to find U001-7883. It is the same programme or order for the military police, the same content, dated the 13th of May, 1998. We have the original of that document in the Albanian language, U001-7883. I'd ask that those be put before the witness. They have been passed out to all present in the courtroom. And we have then on Sanction as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But also at this time - I think it might be helpful to do it now for the witness - could the witness be given the document behind tab 16. That's U000-7849, dated 14 July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, sir, is that programme for military police, both dated 13th May, 1998, the one you've got before you now and the one which His Honour was asking you questions about, is that the same order, the same programme?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me. If I might, Mr. Nicholls. I believe that the original document is entitled somewhat differently than the translation. The translation is entitled "Programme for Military Police." And I certainly do not speak Albanian, but it is clear that the original has the words "Plan, Programme." And then after that I'm not sure. I'm assuming that that's something "police," and the last word I'm assuming is "military." So I think just for purposes of clarification of the record it's important to recognise that there is from the outset a distinction between the title of the two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: General, please tell us, looking at the original in your version, what is the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title of this document is "Plan, Programme of the Military Police."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, on U001-7883, there's a signature at the bottom on the original over your typed name. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my signature. I don't know whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you read the signature in your language? Can you read the name?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The signature is of Shaban Shala, signed by him. But this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who is Shaban Shala?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shaban Shala has been a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was he a subordinate of yours?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he -- he's never been my subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this juncture, for the sake of clarification, I would find it extremely useful, and it's my application that the provenance of this document be established. Of course, this is a document which has not been exhibited. It's a document that we know nothing about its origins and -- from my learned friends that it may have come from the Serbs. But I think provenance ought to be established be it as a condition precedent to its formal admission. In any event, it goes to weight, of course. But, Your Honour, perhaps that clarification can be given now for the assistance of the Court and of course of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Khan, the provenance of the document will be an issue for its admission into evidence and for any significance in the end to be attached to it. Its content though is such that the issues that are now being examined need to be examined while the witness is here. And I think that's what we need to do now. And what can be made of it later will be in the hands perhaps of other witnesses as to its prominence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course your point is, as always, well made and well taken. My point was, rather -- at the moment the document has just appeared, as it were. It hasn't actually been properly admitted. That was the thrust of my observation, Your Honour. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, as you know, in the process that's been followed certainly in this trial, documents have simply been placed by each side before the Chamber, and in the absence of protest, we have been prepared to look at them and act upon them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, often it's very useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But if there is an issue as to provenance, that has to be resolved. Yeah. But we are now -- I wonder whether the 17883 might be given a little prominence on the screen for the moment in its original version, Albanian. Thank you. And as I understand the evidence of the witness, is that this, although appearing above his typed name as "komandant" is in fact -- the document is in fact signed not by him but by another person. And I think that's where we are at, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Where was Shaban Shala stationed in mid-May 1998?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In mid-May 1998, he was probably based at his home place, where he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Was he stationed in mid-1998 in the Drenica region?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Upon my appointment as a zone commander and at the staff headquarters of my zone, he was stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what was his --

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As head of the public relations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what were his responsibilities or duties as head of public relations at that time?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We communicated with the public to deal with issues that the citizens were in need of in the operational zone of Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you ever have written orders or decisions or other documents which you issued as Drenica commander signed for you when you weren't able to sign them yourself?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been possible that someone else might have signed those documents, but when I was present there, I have signed those documents. There was no need for someone else to sign. But I have not been present all the time in this zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And you spoke in your direct testimony that you gave oral orders and written orders and that you would follow up oral orders later on with written orders or decisions. So just to clarify. You've said if you weren't -- there was no need for you to sign [sic] if you were present. If you weren't present, what would the procedure be?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably my subordinate or the chief of the staff who was my subordinate, then he would sign those documents. I'm talking about the operational issues. As about the civil issues or organisational issues, there were various sectors who were in charge of those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'd like you to look at another document, U000-7849 is the English translation. U000-7849 is also the ERN number assigned to the Albanian original. In the English, the title of this document is "Announcement." It's dated 14 July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is behind tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you take a look at that document, sir, tell me after you've familiarised yourself with it if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Is -- I think I have the -- the proper document. Is that 7849, did you say? Yes, it --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We seem to be moving on to another topic, one that is outside the questions asked by the Court as well as the questions that were generated by Mr. Powles with regard to issues concerning military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think, if Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on that basis, since the subject matter we have been addressing is that of military police, I would object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Your submission, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This goes directly to the other issue raised by my friend, the authentication of the other document. This is a related issue. I think it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're saying you're dealing -- going to this document purely on the question of signature and authentication; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're not going otherwise to deal with the content of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, the content is not at issue. The issue is the practice at that time and the signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On that basis, Mr. Guy-Smith, I would allow the question. Or questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, to the extent that we're now dealing with the -- the specific time frame of July, I have no objection. If Mr. Nicholls seeks to go back in time by utilising this document, I do have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Time will tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at the document, General?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Whose signature is it above your typed name at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the signature of the same person. It is clearly seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That same person, for the record, being Shaban Shala?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what else is written next to your name at the bottom of the document in your language other than the signature of Shaban Shala?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that it is written the name "commander." It is my name and it is signed by Shaban Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. And what is written just before your name? There's a small piece of handwriting to the left of your first name.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written "For Shaban Shala."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. And do you remember -- well, I'll leave that. Do you recognize the signature there?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which signature are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Shaban Shala's.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is -- I don't know whether this is his signature or not, but this is what -- what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When documents were signed for you, would you after -- what would you do after that with those documents? Would you review those documents?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not clear to me what you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to be a bit more specific. If an order or a document or a programme is signed in your name, as we saw one yesterday, or if one is signed for you, is there any difference to the weight of those documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that question certainly goes far afield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're ahead of me, but we're on the same tack --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Guy-Smith. I think we can leave that question without an answer, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll move to admit this document, U008-7849.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For the purpose of signature only, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to move all three in, Your Honour, for the purpose, yes, of the signature and for the practice that the documents -- it's another document signed for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You just said "all three." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I intend to admit both versions of the "Programme for Police."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, can we say that on the issue of signature of an announcement from the Drenica operational headquarters the document at 16, ending 849, would be admitted; the documents at 13 are the subject of a yet unresolved dispute as to provenance. They would be -- at the moment they would be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, if we could provisionally admit tab 13, Your Honour, and also the clearer copy which we've provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That should have a separate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On the basis indicated, the document at tab 16 will be -- which is an announcement dated the 14th of July, 1998, from the Drenica operational headquarters, will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit No. P94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the plan, programme for military police, dated 13 May 1998 of the Drenica headquarters will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just for the record - and I apologise for standing - just a clarification. My learned friend says that they were sought to be exhibited as another document signed for him, meaning, I suppose, signed for this witness. Your Honour, of course, there's no evidence that it has in fact been signed for this witness, and the record should be clear on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P95, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Additionally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what document is that? The better quality original; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of MFI P95.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P95.1 MFI, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: For the record as well, Your Honour, these documents that we provided during the break have been disclosed previously to the Defence, as well as having been provided copies just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Now, is there anything further --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To ensure Mr. Nicholls that there's no issue with regard to late disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I may ask one or two additional questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: General Selimi, in May of 1998, when you signed or otherwise issued written orders, documents, how were they disseminated?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the end of May 1998 -- you're talking about that period?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's say all of May 1998. If there was a change, you can explain what it was. How were documents from you disseminated as necessary during that period?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think based upon this particular witness's testimony, that characterisation, meaning all of May of 1998, may be a mis -- a bit misleading and confusing to the Trial Chamber, and I would suggest that this witness has made it clear as to when he obtained his position as commander or commandant, and therefore his written orders would be occurring not throughout May of 1998 but during a certain period of that month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your observation that the date is clear is perhaps a little ambitious, but I agree there is a change of status sometime around May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm working for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's my concern, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you issued decisions, let's say, mid-May 1998, how were they disseminated?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends whether I was there and then they were disseminated right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did you ever have to deliver or have delivered written decisions to several places, several units?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, if you had a written decision, you'd made a written order that applied to several units, how would they receive that order? Try to remember.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would be notified. All the brigade commanders and the unit commander would have been notified about that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And let me try it this way: One of the documents we looked at yesterday or the day before. Did you ever have to make multiple copies of documents in order to place them in different areas, in archives or to be delivered to different places and stored?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I do not remember. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Were copies or were documents ever -- that were intended for units. Were copies ever also delivered to the Main -- to the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, if that was possible, if that was necessary, would the document be typed up multiple times and signed by you multiple times, or did you have sort of any copying facilities available?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, with regard to that question, Mr. Nicholls has taken two distinct concepts and included it in one question, which makes it a misleading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A valid comment. Becoming a bit of a habit by, I think, every counsel so far though.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Did you have copying facilities at that time? And I'll talk now about May 1998.

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We had some at the time, but at the beginning we had only a typewriter and later we had some facilities for some time and then they were burned during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When you only had the typewriter, if you remember, were multiple copies of the same document ever typed up?

utterances.speaker: SYLEJMAN SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I looked along the Defence table then in case any counsel felt that there was need for any further exploration of any issue. I see no inclination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: General, I'm pleased to be able to tell you that that is the end of your questioning. The Chamber is grateful for your assistance and thanks you for having come to the Tribunal to assist the Chamber. You are now, of course, free to return to Kosovo. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too. It was my pleasure to express here what I feel and what I've experienced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls -- oh, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll address this. Unfortunately, Your Honour, the Prosecution doesn't have available another witness for this week as the result of a scheduling problem. We will have our next witness available on Monday, and thereafter we'll endeavour to fill every week as best we can. But our apologies for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we had received some indication, I think, yesterday that this may be an issue. In the circumstances, the appropriate course would appear to be to adjourn now until Monday, bearing in mind that Friday was a holiday in any event. That being so, we will resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 24th day of January, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.51 p.m.,
